# ACTS Workflow Conventions
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

Use this file as the source for building new ACTS workspaces and workflows. Apply the repository's `AGENTS.md` identity and output rules first. A configured workflow may add domain rules in its own references, but must not silently weaken these contracts. Existing non-ACTS workspaces keep their own contracts until migrated.

## Context And Sources

| Layer | Location | Job |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Repository and workflow `AGENTS.md` | Identity and operating behavior |
| 1 | Workflow `CONTEXT.md` | User-intent routing and what to load |
| 2 | Selected stage `CONTEXT.md` | Interface, gates, and verification |
| 3 | `_config/`, `references/`, stage `references/` | Stable rules and reusable knowledge |
| 4 | `{{RUN_PATH}}/` and declared external sources | Current-run inputs, source pointers, state, and generated artifacts |

- Read the router, then the selected stage contract. Load only the Layer 3 and 4 files and sections declared by that stage. State `Full file` when needed; do not scan other stages by default.
- Keep routers brief. Put substantive rules in `_config/` or `references/`, and link to them from routing and stage inputs.
- Use a `CONTEXT.md` router within a large reference collection when it helps select only the needed section.
- Give each stable rule or fact one authoritative home; other files point to it. Reference documents govern how to build; older outputs are evidence or continuation inputs, not templates for new work.
- Use `_config/stage-registry.md` as the sole owner of ordered roles and configured Measure and Learn paths. Do not repeat those paths in routers or quality policy.
- Layers 0-3 define the reusable machine; Layer 4 is the current run. Keep stable references out of run folders. Keep resolved run-specific source pointers, values, and outputs out of reusable workflow folders. External sources stay in place and are named in the run manifest and, when required, stage input records. A stage can consume another stage's output only when it declares that dependency.
- Stable reference dependencies point one way. Declared quality corrections, prior-cycle handoffs, and resume routes may point back to production; do not create hidden circular source dependencies.

## Stage And Routing Contracts

- Assemble workflows through independent setup operations: Define content and future run schemas, Build one Stage, Build Router, Build Agent, Add Quality, Validate. Run only the operation needed; do not execute production before validation passes.
- Every executable stage declares `Inputs -> One Transformation -> Outputs`. Its inputs table names source, file or location, required scope, and why it is needed. Its outputs table names artifact, path, format, and consumer.
- Include an input gate, process, output verification, and review or approval gate when applicable. These support the contract; no fixed heading order is required. Stop when a required input is absent or invalid.
- Route a user request to the smallest stage that can complete it. Use one or more production stages followed by a quality-gate stage and a next-action stage (Measure and Learn by default).
- The final production stage writes `build-handoff.md` naming the outputs and exact paths that Measure audits. Measure writes `audit-findings.md`; Learn writes `what-now.md` only after the gate passes.
- Local verification failures are corrected in the responsible stage. A failed final gate returns findings to the smallest responsible production stage, re-runs dependent stale stages, and returns to Measure. Follow `_config/quality-policy.md` for scoring and recovery.
- Add a human checkpoint when judgment materially affects downstream creative work; stop for explicit approval before commitments or irreversible actions. Apply `_config/review-policy.md`.
- For creative and build stages, define specific local audit checks when they help prevent errors. Agree on intended value before a creative build when the output's usefulness depends on it. See `references/specialized-conventions.md` for domain-specific patterns.

## Names And Run Outputs

- Use lowercase hyphenated file and folder names; no spaces. Use `{{SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE}}` placeholders. Number sequential stage folders with zero-padded prefixes (`01-`, `02-`); independent capabilities may use descriptive names.
- Give generated deliverables stable, descriptive names; use `[topic-slug]-[artifact-type].md` when a topic distinguishes runs. Keep control handoffs named `build-handoff.md`, `audit-findings.md`, and `what-now.md`.
- Before starting a run, confirm `{{OUTPUT_ROOT}}` and propose `{{RUN_PATH}} = {{OUTPUT_ROOT}}/{{WORKSPACE_SLUG}}/{{RUN_SLUG}}`. Generate a short slug from the request. The run path must not be inside the reusable workflow definition. Never overwrite an earlier run by default.
- For a project-hosted run, the confirmed project output root is `{{OUTPUT_ROOT}}`.
- Put the run manifest, optional resolved input records, and generated stage artifacts under `{{RUN_PATH}}/`; keep `run-manifest.md` and `run-state.md` at the run root. A stage's reusable folder contains contracts and stable input schemas under `references/`, not populated input records or generated results. Use `_config/run-manifest-template.md` and `_config/run-input-template.md` for blank runtime record shapes.
- The manifest records the workflow, date, request, confirmed inputs, and links to earlier or external runs when used. On a later cycle ask whether it is new or a continuation; link the prior run and read `what-now.md` only when the receiving stage declares it. For an external handoff record source workspace, run path, and identifiers when available; do not invent them.
- Use workspace-relative paths for reusable references, without `{{RUN_PATH}}`. The stage resolves the confirmed run path at execution time. Update run state before blocking, pausing, resuming, or completing; use `_config/run-state-template.md`.
- A status request for a run reads its manifest, state, and declared outputs. Do not infer completion from files in reusable stage folders.

## Maintenance

- Fix one-off output defects at the responsible stage. For recurring defects, update the authoritative rule, reference, or route.
- On a structural change update the router and affected contracts; on an interface change update both producer and consumer. Re-run only stages made stale by changed inputs or rules.
- Keep instructions short and plain: target under 100 lines for a `CONTEXT.md` and under 200 lines per reference. Split longer material by topic. Keep output style and AI attribution under the governing `AGENTS.md`.
